p01.challenge_claim: The row files its dod signal under the beloved address vocabulary when the span's only dod-family bytes are the DEFECTIVE 'your loves' object, and three further attributions - verse position, marker location, cross-verse constancy - are imprecise against the bytes.
p01.grounds: Re-derived object-first, not digit-first. The span's only dod-skeleton bytes are דֹּדֶ֖יךָ (oshb:Song.1.2, tier: byte) and דֹדֶ֨יךָ֙ (oshb:Song.1.4, tier: byte); both skeletonize to the vav-less spelling, which is the DEFECTIVE 'your loves' object (sweep: 4 verses - MT 1:2, MT 1:4, MT 4:10, MT 7:13 [= WEB 7:12]), and I re-checked both address lists: neither MT 1:2 nor MT 1:4 appears in dodi-exact (24 verses) or dod-family (28 verses). So the signal key naming the dodi address vocabulary names an object this span does not carry - the tier-1 dod address-epithet - which is the five-object blend in its field-level form. Verse position confirmed: the span is Song.1.2-Song.1.4, so oshb:Song.1.4 is its THIRD verse, not its second. Marker location confirmed: in מָשְׁכֵ֖נִי אַחֲרֶ֣יךָ (oshb:Song.1.4, tier: byte) the 2ms marker is the final kaf of אַחֲרֶ֣יךָ; the imperative's own suffix is 1cs, so 'imperative-plus-suffix address' mislocates it (the imperative STEM is 2ms at the pointed-byte tier, which is why this is a wording defect rather than a false attribution). Cross-verse constancy confirmed: MT 1:3 carries the span's densest 2ms evidence - שְׁמָנֶ֣יךָ, שְׁמֶ֑ךָ, אֲהֵבֽוּךָ (all tier: byte at oshb:Song.1.3) - and the row splices none of it, while בָּ֔ךְ (oshb:Song.1.4, tier: byte) is 2fs in form and 2ms only on a pausal reading, left undisclosed and genuinely unsettleable with no morphology layer staged. ONE CORRECTION to the challenge's own framing: the row's boundary argument does not lean on the dod key - its stated tier-1 evidence is the 2ms suffix forms - so the blend is a field-contract defect, not a failed voice attribution.
p01.remedy: Re-key observed_substrate_signals off the dodi address vocabulary to the gendered-form signal class the row actually argues; in boundary_rationale NAME the swept object before any dod word (the defective 'your loves' spelling, sweep: 4 verses); correct 'second verse' to 'third verse'; re-word the MT 1:4 marker as the 2ms suffix on אַחֲרֶ֣יךָ (spliced, tier: byte) rather than on the imperative's suffix; splice at least one 2ms form from oshb:Song.1.3 (tier: byte) into the three-verse continuity claim; disclose בָּ֔ךְ as form-2fs / pausal-2ms and unsettleable. CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): any dod reference in this row must survive a name-the-object check against the dodi-exact (24 verses) and dod-family (28 verses) lists, neither of which contains MT 1:2 or MT 1:4.

p01.challenge_claim: The row's closing-seam driver is byte-false in position and is voice-identity rather than voice-shift evidence, and no Hebrew at all is quoted from MT 1:6.
p01.grounds: All three arms re-derived and confirmed. MT 1:7 opens הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֗י (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte; that opener is 1 verse book-wide), and שֶׁ֤אָהֲבָה֙ נַפְשִׁ֔י (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte) stands as the verse's third and fourth tokens - so 'the she-ahavah-nafshi formula opening Song.1.7' is byte-false in position. Substantively: that formula is tier-1 under the moderate policy but it is HER formula at all five of its verses (sweep: 5 verses - MT 1:7, 3:1, 3:2, 3:3, 3:4) and MT 1:5-1:6 is her voice as well, so across MT 1:6|1:7 it marks voice IDENTITY, not a voice shift; it cannot be the closing driver the row makes it. The seam is real and byte-markable as an ADDRESSEE shift the row never quotes: plural אַל תִּרְא֨וּנִי֙ (oshb:Song.1.6, tier: byte) addressing the daughters, against 2ms חֲבֵרֶֽיךָ (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte) addressing the man. With no Hebrew spliced from MT 1:6, the row's 'no further addressee change through the end of Song.1.6' rests on the English rendering alone. Tier-4 audit: no modern voice-apparatus heading precedes WEB 1:7, so this seam is not apparatus-derived - the row is clean on that axis. PEER-SIDE FINDING carried forward: the converging primary SUPPORTED this row on precisely the arm that fails, reproducing the byte-false 'formula opening Song.1.7' position - the support item is itself defective.
p01.remedy: Replace the closing driver: argue MT 1:6|1:7 from the addressee flip, splicing אַל תִּרְא֨וּנִי֙ (oshb:Song.1.6, tier: byte) against חֲבֵרֶֽיךָ (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte), each tier-labeled; demote the she-ahavah-nafshi formula to what it is here - a same-voice tier-1 anchor confirming her voice continues - and correct the position claim (the opener is הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֗י). CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): the replacement driver must show a marked change ACROSS the seam; a formula attested only in her voice cannot mark a shift out of her voice.

p01.challenge_claim: The single-verse holding is byte-sound, but the formula's byte position is misstated and the 2ms gender claim is asserted on a morphologically ambiguous form whose in-verse disambiguator is never quoted.
p01.grounds: Both arms are byte-confirmed, but the severity is understated - the corrected finding is medium, not low. תִרְעֶ֔ה (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte) is a prefix-conjugation form whose 2ms and 3fs readings are graphically identical, and no morphology layer is staged, so the row's 'carries second-masculine-singular marking' is not a byte claim at all. The 2ms reading is in fact secure - fixed by חֲבֵרֶֽיךָ (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte) in the same verse, with תַּרְבִּ֣יץ (tier: byte) in parallel - so the CONCLUSION survives while its cited evidence does not. That matters more than 'low': this is the cluster's only single-verse holding, it is filed at HIGH confidence, and its entire rejected alternative rests on a masculine-to-feminine gender flip at MT 1:7|1:8 whose masculine side is asserted on the ambiguous form. Position arm confirmed as in the preceding row (the opener is הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֗י). Third arm confirmed: 'flips every verb and suffix' is a universal with no adjacent digit and no spliced form, while MT 1:8 in fact carries 6 such markers; the machine universals arm independently flags this sentence. TWO further peer findings: (a) this byte-false formula position appears in TWO rows of this cluster, so it is a CURE CLASS and the correction must be swept, not spot-fixed; (b) the converging primary supported this row asserting the 2ms verb was 'confirmed at byte tier' - a byte confirmation the staged extract cannot yield for this form.
p01.remedy: Splice חֲבֵרֶֽיךָ (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte) as the disambiguator that fixes the 2ms reading, and re-cast תִרְעֶ֔ה as form-ambiguous between 2ms and 3fs with no morphology layer staged; correct the formula's position; give the MT 1:8 flip a digit and at least one spliced 2fs form (6 markers at oshb:Song.1.8). Sweep the position correction across every row of this cluster that repeats it. CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): every gender claim must rest on a form unambiguous at the pointed-byte tier, or be explicitly held.

p01.challenge_claim: The row argues a four-verse single-addressee unit while leaving the one tier-1 address anchor inside its own span uncited and carrying three of its four verses on the English rendering alone.
p01.grounds: Confirmed. רַעְיָתִֽי (oshb:Song.1.9, tier: byte) sits INSIDE this row's own span and is the attested tier-1 address anchor of his word for her (sweep: 9 verses - MT 1:9, 1:15, 2:2, 2:10, 2:13, 4:1, 4:7, 5:2, 6:4), re-checked against the inventory; the row neither argues MT 1:9 in prose nor mirrors it into boundary_evidence_refs, and it is the single strongest available warrant for the row's own male-voice reading. The 2fs object suffix on דִּמִּיתִ֖יךְ (oshb:Song.1.9, tier: byte) goes unused with it. Translation-carrying confirmed: no Hebrew is spliced from MT 1:9, MT 1:10 or MT 1:11 - three of the four verses of a four-verse continuity claim. Negation slip confirmed: MT 1:8 opens אִם לֹ֤א (tier: byte), so תֵדְעִי֙ (tier: byte) is neither the unit's opening token nor the bearer of the negation the row's gloss puts inside it. The credit is also correct and I re-audited it: a modern voice-apparatus heading does precede WEB 1:11, and the row declines it on the absence of a gender-marked form - that arm audits clean against apparatus-leaning. PEER-SIDE ADDITION, unraised by either primary: the row's English for MT 1:10 and MT 1:11 stands in straight quotes with a bare numeric ref while carrying verses that have no Hebrew at all, which routes WEB renderings around the curly-quote-plus-inline-web-ref requirement.
p01.remedy: Add oshb:Song.1.9 to boundary_evidence_refs and splice רַעְיָתִֽי (tier: byte) into boundary_rationale as the span's tier-1 address anchor, with the object named and its digit (sweep: 9 verses); splice at least one 2fs form from oshb:Song.1.10 and from oshb:Song.1.11 (tier: byte) so the four-verse continuity stops being translation-carried; re-cut the gloss of תֵדְעִי֙ so the negation sits where the bytes put it, and stop calling it the opening token. In the same pass repair the quote convention: any WEB rendering carried as evidence takes curly quotes plus an inline web: ref in the SAME field. CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): every verse inside the span must carry at least one spliced tier-labeled form or an explicit hold - MT 1:9, which carries the span's own tier-1 anchor, failed it.

p01.challenge_claim: A voice-shift seam is asserted with no gender-marked form quoted on either side of it, and two of the book's twelve paseq verses sit inside this three-verse span undisclosed.
p01.grounds: Arm 1 upheld; arms 2 and 3 do not survive re-derivation. ARM 1 CONFIRMED: the row asserts a shift out of 2fs address into her first-person voice at MT 1:11|1:12 and splices no Hebrew on either side of it. The 2fs form at the seam is נַעֲשֶׂה לָּ֔ךְ (oshb:Song.1.11, tier: byte); MT 1:12's only first-person marker is נִרְדִּ֖י (tier: byte), a gender-UNMARKED 1cs possessive standing beside third-person שֶׁ֤הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ (tier: byte, the melek lexeme - sweep: 5 verses). The row's two spliced quotes sit one and two verses past the seam, so the seam is carried by tier-2 continuity while the moderate policy requires the gender-marked form to be quoted at a voice-shift seam - a real medium defect. ARM 2 REFUTED: the paseq layer is a count-only seg inventory, and the unconditional span-relevant disclosure symmetry runs over the PARASHAH set, not over paseq; this row's span-relevant parashah obligation (the SAMEKH at MT 1:14) IS disclosed, and the marks arm returns clean over the whole cluster. A row that makes no paseq claim owes no paseq disclosure, so there is no symmetry gap here. ARM 3 REFUTED on the bytes: the row NAMES its object ('the dodi-exact form') and 24 verses is that object's correct count, with MT 1:13 and MT 1:14 both on the list; the adjacent two-word run is a separate object (byte tier: 2 verses, MT 1:13 and MT 1:14; skeleton tier: 4 verses, adding MT 2:16 and MT 6:3), but the row attaches NO digit to that run, so there is an invitation to slippage and no actual blend to cure. PEER-SIDE FINDING, unraised by either primary: the row's sole stated evidence for its opening verse is an English string attached to a web: ref that is not that verse's WEB rendering at all - a mis-attributed rendering standing where a splice or a verbatim quote belongs.
p01.remedy: Splice נַעֲשֶׂה לָּ֔ךְ (oshb:Song.1.11, tier: byte) and נִרְדִּ֖י (oshb:Song.1.12, tier: byte) into the seam argument, tier-labeled, and re-cast the seam honestly: the marked 2fs addressee DROPS and no gender-marked first-person form replaces it, so the shift rests on the disappearance of the marked addressee plus tier-2 continuity, with confidence held accordingly. Replace the English at the opening verse with either that verse's verbatim WEB rendering in curly quotes with its inline web: ref, or a spliced tier-labeled Hebrew quote. Leave the paseq segs and the 24-verse digit untouched - both are already correct. CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): the seam sentence must quote a form from EACH side of MT 1:11|1:12 and must not claim a gender-marked shift the bytes do not carry.

p01.challenge_claim: The exchange's opening is the cluster's best byte evidence, but its closing seam at MT 2:3|2:4 carries no byte evidence, no forward neighbour ref, and is crossed by an unbroken single-speaker configuration the row never discloses.
p01.grounds: Confirmed at byte tier. The opening is sound - הִנָּ֤ךְ (oshb:Song.1.15, tier: byte, 2fs) against הִנְּךָ֨ (oshb:Song.1.16, tier: byte, 2ms) is exactly the gender-marked pair the moderate policy asks for. The closing seam is not argued at all: no sentence of the row addresses MT 2:3|2:4, and boundary_evidence_refs carries only a backward neighbour (WEB 1:14), no forward one. The bytes run straight across the cut: 1cs חִמַּ֣דְתִּי and וְיָשַׁ֔בְתִּי with לְחִכִּֽי (oshb:Song.2.3, tier: byte) continue into הֱבִיאַ֨נִי֙ with 3ms וְדִגְל֥וֹ and עָלַ֖י (oshb:Song.2.4, tier: byte) - same speaker configuration, no vocative, no address-vocabulary token, no gender-marked addressee change at the cut. A byte-true single-voice run straddling the row's own seam argues continuity AGAINST the row unless disclosed, and it is undisclosed; under the hybrid granularity rule a cut inside a sustained single-voice run needs a tier-1 marker at the cut, and there is none. Secondary arms hold: the row keeps MT 1:17 inside her turn on the English rendering with no Hebrew spliced, and the token it leans on is the qere in the span's one K/Q-bearing verse (4 K/Q notes book-wide, single-witness) that the row simultaneously declares it makes no K/Q claim about; and אֲנִי֙ חֲבַצֶּ֣לֶת (oshb:Song.2.1, tier: byte) is gender-unmarked and left unattributed inside a unit whose entire warrant is attributed alternation. CONVERGENCE: this is the SAME core defect as the other primary's item on this row, reached from different evidence - see that ruling.
p01.remedy: (a) BOUNDARY PROPOSAL, explicit boss adoption required - extend the exchange to close at the MT 2:6|2:7 refrain bracket, or re-cut so the single-voice run beginning inside MT 2:3 is not severed. (b) If the cut at MT 2:3|2:4 is retained, disclose the cross-seam single-voice continuity explicitly, add the forward neighbour to boundary_evidence_refs, and lower the confidence. (c) Splice the 1cp forms עַרְשֵׂ֖נוּ (oshb:Song.1.16, tier: byte) and בָּתֵּ֨ינוּ֙ (oshb:Song.1.17, tier: byte) in place of the English for the MT 1:17 arm, and note the qere status of the other 1cp token in that verse. (d) Attribute MT 2:1 at the tier the bytes support, or record it as held. CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): the far boundary must name a tier-1 marker AT the cut, or the row must disclose that none exists and hold its confidence accordingly.

p01.challenge_claim: The far boundary at Song.2.3|Song.2.4 is argued from mirrored ken/ken parallelism rather than any tier-1 voice-shift marker, and the strongest rejected alternative never engages the live rival of extending through Song.2.4-Song.2.6 to the Song.2.7 adjuration close.
p01.grounds: SAME DEFECT as the converging item on this row, not a distinct one: both name the unwarranted far boundary at MT 2:3|2:4, and I have upheld it on byte grounds there. This item's DISTINCT and correct contribution is the rejected-alternative gap: the row's only rival is atomizing into single-verse turns, while the live rival - extending through MT 2:4-2:6 to the adjuration bracket that closes the movement - is never engaged, and it is the rival the hybrid granularity rule makes live at this seam. TWO FRAMING CORRECTIONS. First, this item rests its evidentiary weight on the parashah SAMEKH at MT 2:7, called an 'undisclosed cross-seam corroboration signal': that mark is TIER-3 weak, single-witness, never a boundary driver in either direction, and it does not straddle the MT 2:3|2:4 seam - it sits three verses past it and is not in this row's span-relevant disclosure set, which is the SAMEKH at MT 1:14 and IS disclosed (the marks arm returns clean for this row). Using a tier-3 mark as directional evidence toward a later closure is the same tier error the challenge elsewhere polices. The genuine cross-seam device was available at byte tier: the 1cs configuration of oshb:Song.2.3 running into oshb:Song.2.4. Second, the bar on parallelism standing alone as a boundary driver is a distinct rule from the operative-category law this item cites for it. Net: defect real and upheld, grounds substituted, severity unchanged.
p01.remedy: Covered by the work order on the converging item, plus specifically: strongest_rejected_alternative must engage the extension-to-the-refrain-bracket rival and say from BYTES why it is rejected, or the boundary proposal is adopted instead - one sentence, plus the optional second sentence only for the mandated rival disclosure. CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): the rejected alternative must name the rival the granularity rule makes live at this seam, not only the rival the row can easily refute.

p01.challenge_claim: The Song.2.4 opening is argued from the absence of a formula anchor past Song.2.3 rather than from a positive tier-1 marker, so the row theme-splits a maximal she-voice run that properly spans Song.2.3-Song.2.7; the row's signal entry names a dodi anchor that stands in no verse of its own span; and the Song.2.6 WEB citation is straight-quoted and lower-cases the source's verse-initial word.
p01.grounds: Diagnosis upheld, corrected span refuted. Upheld on bytes: nothing at the 2:3|2:4 junction is a tier-1 in-verse marker -- the last clause of oshb:Song.2.3 and the opening verb of oshb:Song.2.4 hold the same first-person speaker and the same third-masculine-singular referent, with no vocative, no suffix flip and no address-vocabulary anchor AT the cut, so the row's stated driver is anchor-absence plus a topic change (tier-2 continuity reasoning at best, not the tier-1 ground the hybrid granularity rule demands at a cut). Upheld on bytes: the row quotes the Song.2.6 clause with straight delimiters and lower-cases the verse-initial word -- that witness reads “His right hand embraces me.” (web:Song.2.6), and the row's string fails an exact-case substring check while passing case-insensitively; zero curly-quoted WEB runs stand anywhere in this cluster's rows. REFUTED, with the refuting bytes: the corrected span the challenge proposes (Song.2.3-Song.2.7) cannot stand. Song.2.3 is the answering member of an attested tier-1 alternation pair -- רַעְיָתִ֖י (oshb:Song.2.2, tier: byte), his address word for her, answered by דּוֹדִ֖י (oshb:Song.2.3, tier: byte), her word for him -- inside the hinnakh/hinnekha exchange that the owner ruling holds whole as one dialogue unit; moving Song.2.3 into a she-voice run would both break that whole-held zone and split an attested anchor pair. The seam is therefore real and inherited from the preceding zone's close; only the row's STATEMENT of it is defective. Signal-entry sub-claim REFINED, not upheld: no dod-family token stands in Song.2.4-Song.2.6 (verified verse by verse), so the challenge's byte observation is right, but the signal field contract records the signal CLASS consulted, and consulting the address-vocabulary class to establish that no anchor survives is within the contract -- the defect is the rationale's reliance on that absence, not the field entry. NEW FINDING (neither primary): the ahavah citation blends units -- the row calls the Song.2.4 form a token and then says 'one of ten', while the true objects are 10 VERSES and 11 TOKENS (MT 8:7 carries two); the parenthetical names verses, the prose object does not.
p01.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the anchor-absence driver with the positive warrant that the preceding unit is a whole-held dialogue exchange closing at Song.2.3, citing the attested anchor pair (his address word at oshb:Song.2.2, hers at oshb:Song.2.3, tier: byte) as the reason this row opens at Song.2.4; delete the 'no formula anchor survives past Song.2.3' phrasing as a driver. Re-cut the Song.2.6 citation as a curly-quoted, exact-case run paired with its inline web: ref. device_notes: name the swept object and unit for the ahavah claim (10 verses, 11 tokens). Tests the cure must pass: the span must still open at Song.2.4 (a re-cut to Song.2.3 fails the whole-held dialogue-zone rule and splits the oshb:Song.2.2/oshb:Song.2.3 anchor pair -- this is the test that kills the challenge's own proposed replacement); the WEB run must pass an exact-case contiguous substring check against that witness; the ahavah citation must name object and unit before its digit. Span change: none proposed.

p01.challenge_claim: No tier-1 marker stands at the row's opening cut; an undisclosed apple-token link straddles that same seam; the row's no-addressee ground is contradicted by the imperatives in its own middle verse and is inconsistent with the criterion applied at Song.2.15; and the closing seam is argued only from an English rendering while the embrace colon's recurrence before the later adjuration goes undisclosed.
p01.grounds: Three sub-findings upheld exactly on re-derivation, one re-labelled. (1) Same defect as the LF item at the cut: verified, no tier-1 in-verse marker at 2:3|2:4. (2) Cross-seam token link verified with the object named: the stem shared by the two apple forms sweeps to 4 verses at skeleton tier (MT 2:3, MT 2:5, MT 7:9 = WEB 7:8, MT 8:5 -- the offset-zone dual is arithmetically right), two of them on opposite sides of this row's own opening seam, and both witnesses carry the link; the row discloses nothing. The tier is skeleton, not byte: the two attested forms differ in number and pointing, so the honest statement is a shared-stem link, not a formula recurrence. (3) The no-addressee ground is byte-false INSIDE the row's own span: סַמְּכ֨וּנִי֙ בָּֽאֲשִׁישׁ֔וֹת רַפְּד֖וּנִי (oshb:Song.2.5, tier: byte) is two plural imperatives carrying first-person-singular object suffixes -- an explicit addressee -- and that other witness renders them as imperatives too; the inconsistency charge also holds, since the plural-imperative-addressee feature is what drives the cut at Song.2.15 in this same cluster. (4) RE-LABELLED inside the uphold: the byte fact is verified -- וִימִינ֖וֹ תְּחַבְּקֵֽנִי (oshb:Song.2.6, tier: byte) recurs at MT 8:3 at SKELETON tier only (skeleton sweep of that colon: 2 verses, MT 2:6 and MT 8:3; the byte and accent tiers each return 1 verse because the later site carries an extra meteg, and the verse's left-hand colon differs by a prefixed preposition and sweeps to 1 verse, which is how the pair escapes an exact sweep) -- and it stands immediately before the MT 8:4 adjuration, so an embrace-line-then-adjuration sequence recurs; but that parallel SUPPORTS this row's own 2:6|2:7 close rather than arguing a rival to it, so it is an undisclosed strengthener, not a rival cut. The closing-seam complaint stands on its own: the seam is argued from an English rendering with no Hebrew quoted at the closing verse.
p01.remedy: boundary_rationale: delete the no-addressee ground outright and re-state the span's texture from its own bytes (a first-person voice that includes an addressed plural imperative at Song.2.5); ground the closing seam in Hebrew by quoting the embrace colon from oshb:Song.2.6 (tier: byte) rather than in translation. device_notes: disclose the apple-stem link across the opening seam with its tier and digit (skeleton sweep: 4 verses, MT 2:3, MT 2:5, MT 7:9 = WEB 7:8, MT 8:5), and disclose the embrace-colon recurrence at MT 8:3 (skeleton sweep: 2 verses) as a parallel supporting this close. Reconcile the plural-imperative criterion with its use as a cut driver at Song.2.15 in one clause. Tests the cure must pass: no stated ground may survive that the row's own span bytes contradict (the Song.2.5 imperatives are the test that killed the original); every cross-seam device named must carry tier AND digit AND its offset-zone dual where one applies; the same feature must not be a driver in one row and absent from the criterion in another. Span change: none proposed.

p01.challenge_claim: LF: the Song.2.14 WEB citation is verbatim in content but straight-quoted rather than curly, a register-only defect. OL: the frame-verb wording attributed to web:Song.2.10 is not that witness's rendering, and the blossom-token chain straddling the closing seam is undisclosed; the second-feminine-singular marker case and the disclosure symmetry are otherwise the cluster's strongest.
p01.grounds: DISTINCT defects. The refinement is of severity and of which finding is load-bearing: the LF item rates this row's only defect 'low' and register-only, which understates the row, because the substantive defect it missed is a misattributed witness rendering. Verified: the row gives the frame verb as an answered-and-said wording attributed to web:Song.2.10, but that witness reads “My beloved spoke, and said to me,” (web:Song.2.10) -- the row's string fails a substring check against that witness even case-insensitively, so the wording ascribed to the cited witness is not its wording. The Hebrew עָנָ֥ה דוֹדִ֖י וְאָ֣מַר לִ֑י (oshb:Song.2.10, tier: byte) does support an answered-gloss, but this row quotes no Hebrew at that clause, so its own frame-verb ground is translation-dependent on a rendering that witness does not carry. LF's register point is separately verified and real: the Song.2.14 run is an exact-case verbatim substring of that witness but is delimited with straight marks, and this cluster carries zero curly-quoted WEB runs while the corpus uses the curly convention elsewhere -- so the departure is local, not a book-wide convention. OL's cross-seam finding verified with object and tier: the blossom token is byte at each of its own sites, סְמָדַ֖ר (oshb:Song.2.13, tier: byte) and סְמָדַֽר (oshb:Song.2.15, tier: byte), and the link between them is skeleton tier, sweeping to 3 verses book-wide (MT 2:13, MT 2:15, MT 7:13 = WEB 7:12 -- dual arithmetically right), two of the three sitting on opposite sides of this row's closing cut. p01.remedy: Field boundary_rationale (P01-019): delete the parenthetical locating 'my garden' in Song.4.8-Song.4.15 and re-cut the shift to the one attested inside this verse - her spliced 1cs garden form against the 3ms garden form in the same verse, both tier-labeled byte at oshb:Song.4.16 - keeping the her-word-for-him anchor as the tier-1 driver and naming its object (dodi-exact, 24 verses) where any digit is carried. p01.challenge_claim: LF: the Song.2.9 WEB citation ellipsis-splices two non-adjacent clauses, silently drops an intervening sentence, lower-cases a verse-initial word and is straight-quoted, while the row's boundaries are sound. p01.grounds: DISTINCT defects, both upheld; the two primaries did not overlap on this row, and both agree the boundaries themselves are sound (re-derived: the formula opens the movement immediately after the adjuration bracket, and עָנָ֥ה דוֹדִ֖י וְאָ֣מַר לִ֑י (oshb:Song.2.10, tier: byte) is a genuine tier-1 frame verb introducing quoted speech). He looks in at the windows. He glances through the lattice.” (web:Song.2.9), so a whole sentence is dropped inside the ellipsis and the second fragment lower-cases a verse-initial word -- the presented run fails an exact-case check and fails a contiguous check even case-insensitively; delimiters are straight, not curly. OL's bracket upheld with its object verified: the gazelle-and-fawn colon לִצְבִ֔י א֖וֹ לְעֹ֣פֶר הָֽאַיָּלִ֑ים (oshb:Song.2.9, tier: byte) and לִצְבִ֗י א֛וֹ לְעֹ֥פֶר הָאַיָּלִ֖ים (oshb:Song.2.17, tier: byte) share a 19-character consonantal run whose skeleton sweep returns 3 verses (MT 2:9, MT 2:17, MT 8:14); the two chapter-2 members sit on opposite sides of this row's closing seam and bracket MT 2:8-2:17, and no row in the stretch discloses it. Tier-label the qol-dodi recurrence at the tier a collation proves (byte at oshb:Song.2.8; accent_stripped at the second site, attested there in a longer shape), keeping the 2-verse digit. device_notes: disclose the gazelle-and-fawn colon across the closing seam with tier and digit (skeleton sweep: 3 verses, MT 2:9, MT 2:17, MT 8:14) and name the likeness-verb spelling split before any digit is reused. Tests the cure must pass: the WEB run must pass a contiguous exact-case substring check against that witness (the dropped sentence is the test that killed the original); the recurrence claim must carry the tier a collation returns at EVERY cited site, not at the first only; the cross-seam device must be disclosed with tier and digit. Span change: none proposed -- both primaries affirm the boundaries.

p02.challenge_claim: Attributing Song.5.1's garden-report clause to 'the man' crosses the 4:16|5:1 voice seam without quoting the gender-marked formula anchor that grounds it, even though that evidence sits in the same verse the row already cites.
p02.grounds: Verified on the bytes and squarely within the moderate voice-attribution policy. The row rests the man-voice premise on בָּ֣אתִי לְגַנִּי֮ (byte, oshb:Song.5.1), a 1cs perfect that is not gender-marked and cannot by itself carry a voice attribution; the attested tier-1 anchor sits two words later in the same verse, אֲחֹתִ֣י כַלָּה֒ (byte, oshb:Song.5.1), his address vocabulary (bride-epithet form: 5 verses, word-bound, MT 4:9, 4:10, 4:12, 5:1, 5:2; kallah: 6 verses, MT 4:8-4:12 and 5:1), and is never quoted. The policy is explicit that every voice-shift seam claim quotes the gender-marked or attested-anchor Hebrew form, spliced and tier-labeled, and that continuity alone is tier-2 corroboration - so as shipped the cross-part seam is argued at tier-2 while tier-1 evidence lies unquoted inside the row's own span. LF's audit of the row against heading-leaning is correct and worth recording: the tier-4 speaker apparatus is explicitly refused and the plural-summons hedge is held open at the tier the bytes support, so the defect is a missing quotation, not a heading-lean. CONVERGENCE: this row is also challenged by OL. The two items are DISTINCT defects - LF's is the missing in-verse tier-1 anchor for the man-voice premise; OL's is the unanchored cross-part continuity assertion plus two undisclosed byte-true straddles - but they share one root, recorded here as a NEW FINDING neither primary states: the 4:16|5:1 seam is argued from its own bytes by NEITHER row. P01-019 defers the boundary forward ('that reply belongs to the verse immediately following it, argued separately on its own bytes') and P02-001 defers it backward ('closing the movement that opened before this part's own span'), so a seam that IS byte-supportable at tier-1 from both sides - her-word-for-him at oshb:Song.4.16 against his address vocabulary at oshb:Song.5.1 - currently has no tier-1 driver stated in either row. The launch note is right that this is a work-unit boundary and not a literary claim; the mutual deferral is the hazard that boundary created.
p02.remedy: Field boundary_rationale (P02-001), executed as ONE seam-pair edit with P01-019: quote the tier-1 anchor already standing in the verse - his address vocabulary at oshb:Song.5.1, spliced and tier-labeled byte, with its object named (bride-epithet form: 5 verses; kallah: 6 verses, both word-bound) - as the ground for the man's voice, instead of resting it on a 1cs perfect. State the seam positively from both sides so neither row defers it to the other. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS (the test that killed the original): the voice attribution must be carried by a quoted, spliced, tier-labeled gender-marked or attested-anchor form; a 1cs perfect carries no gender and cannot pass, and the cure must not migrate to the tier-4 speaker apparatus, which remains never-evidence in either direction.

p02.challenge_claim: The cross-part continuity the row asserts is left with no byte anchor while two byte-true chains straddle its front seam undisclosed, and the widened-address point leans on the WEB rendering of a dod-family plural the row never names. (severity as filed: low)
p02.grounds: Limbs 1 and 2 verify; limb 3 is largely conceded by OL itself and should not carry weight; severity as filed is too low, because the undisclosed straddles are a mandated disclosure that argues continuity against this row's own front seam at the cross-part boundary - hence refine. Limb 1 UPHELD: the rationale asserts that the verse closes a movement opened before the part's own span while naming no verse and quoting no form, and the front-seam neighbour appears nowhere in boundary_evidence_refs. Limb 2 UPHELD and re-derived: two byte-true chains straddle the front seam undisclosed - יָבֹ֤א דוֹדִי֙ לְגַנּ֔וֹ וְיֹאכַ֖ל (byte, oshb:Song.4.16) answered clause-for-clause by בָּ֣אתִי לְגַנִּי֮ with its eat-verb echo at אָכַ֤לְתִּי (both byte, oshb:Song.5.1), and אֲחֹתִ֣י כַלָּה֒ (byte, oshb:Song.5.1) continuing the man's address vocabulary attested at MT 4:9, 4:10 and 4:12 (bride-epithet form: 5 verses; kallah: 6 verses, word-bound). Standing law makes an undisclosed byte-true cross-seam device an argument for continuity against the row, and here it bears directly on whether Song.5.1 should be held with Song.4.16 at all. Limb 3 REFINED DOWN: the widened-address claim is in fact byte-anchored independently of any rendering by אִכְל֣וּ רֵעִ֔ים (byte, oshb:Song.5.1), which OL concedes; what genuinely remains is that the verse-final דּוֹדִֽים (byte, oshb:Song.5.1) is a dod-family plural, a different object from the 24-verse dodi-exact set of the surrounding verses and the form the closing word of “Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink abundantly, beloved.” (web:Song.5.1) renders - unnamed where the rendering is cited. That is a naming gap, not a leaning defect. CONVERGENCE: distinct from LF's item on this row (missing in-verse tier-1 anchor), with the shared root recorded in that ruling - the 4:16|5:1 seam is argued by neither row on its own bytes. The setumah at MT 5:1 is correctly tiered single-witness and the tier-4 speaker apparatus is explicitly refused.
p02.remedy: Two edits, one row (P02-001), merged with the P02-001/LF edit as one seam-pair cure. (1) boundary_evidence_refs: add the front-seam neighbour (web:Song.4.16 and oshb:Song.4.16), which the continuity assertion argues but does not mirror. (2) device_notes: disclose both straddles - the garden-and-eat answer from oshb:Song.4.16 to oshb:Song.5.1, and the address-vocabulary chain continuing from oshb:Song.4.12 - and state why the possessor change and the addressee change still cut the seam; where the rendering's closing 'beloved' is cited, name the verse-final form as a dod-family plural, distinct from the 24-verse dodi-exact object. TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS: every verse argued in prose outside the row's own span must appear in boundary_evidence_refs; no byte-true device may straddle the row's own seam undisclosed; and the widened-address claim must rest on the spliced plural summons at oshb:Song.5.1, not on the rendering.

p02.challenge_claim: unit_type 'dialogue_exchange' is applied to an atomized single-voice question that contains no alternation, contrary to the category's own definition, and no deviation disclosure is given.
p02.grounds: Re-derived from bytes. MT 5:9 = WEB 5:9 (crosswalk-checked, outside the offset zone) is one uninterrupted chorus turn: the doubled interrogative מַה דּוֹדֵ֣ךְ מִדּ֔וֹד (oshb:Song.5.9, byte tier) occurs twice in-verse and the two runs are byte-identical (byte sweep: 1 verse book-wide, 2 occurrences in-verse), and the verse carries no second turn - the answering wasf is a separate row at web:Song.5.10-Song.5.16. In the closed vocabulary dialogue_exchange is rapid attributed alternation held as ONE unit; a single turn does not carry that form, and the operative-category law that permits any vocabulary value the row's own bytes carry also requires a one-sentence deviation disclosure, which the device note (intra-verse doubling only) does not supply. Tier-1 bounding markers do exist on both edges under the moderate voice policy - the 2fs suffix on דּוֹדֵ֣ךְ (oshb:Song.5.9, byte tier) fixing a female addressee against the 1cs voice of the preceding narrative, and her own answering opener דּוֹדִ֥י (oshb:Song.5.10, byte tier) - which is the lyric_address pattern, not the dialogue_exchange one.
p02.remedy: Re-label unit_type to lyric_address and cite the two tier-1 bounding markers as spliced, tier-labelled forms (the 2fs addressee suffix at oshb:Song.5.9; the answering opener at oshb:Song.5.10); or keep dialogue_exchange and add the mandated one-sentence deviation disclosure in device_notes. observed_substrate_signals is a dependent field and must be re-cut with whichever label survives. Cure test (the test that killed the original): a reviewer reading only the row's own span bytes must find the form the unit_type names - MT 5:9 alone must exhibit alternation if dialogue_exchange is kept. A third cure, widening the span to web:Song.5.9-Song.5.16, is a boundary PROPOSAL only (explicit boss adoption required) and collides with the web:Song.5.10-Song.5.16 wasf bound that both primaries supported.

p02.challenge_claim: The chorus attribution is built on an addressee marker only, dropping the verse's plural-speaker form and the quoted-back oath that straddles the front seam; the attribution 'lands exactly on' the tier-4 WEB voice heading; and the device note contradicts a byte-tier cross-verse recurrence.
p02.grounds: DISTINCT from the LF item on this row, not the same defect: LF challenges the unit_type, OL challenges the evidence base. Two sub-claims verified, two mis-framed. VERIFIED: הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ (oshb:Song.5.9, byte tier) carries the 1cp object suffix and is the only in-verse form that makes the speakers plural; it is uncited, so the PLURAL chorus identification is under-evidenced. VERIFIED: the oath root straddles the row's own front seam - הִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי (oshb:Song.5.8, byte tier) against הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ (oshb:Song.5.9, byte tier), skeleton sweep: 5 verses (MT 2:7, 3:5, 5:8, 5:9, 8:4), the root being oath-only in this book with the speech roles split (adjuration at 5:8; the daughters quoting it back at 5:9) - and the rationale gives a forward reason for the cut only, so the cross-seam cohesion rule is unmet. REFINED (1): that a 2fs suffix 'cannot carry a daughters-attribution' overstates the moderate policy - a 2fs addressee marker set against the 1cs voice of the preceding narrative IS a tier-1 warrant for a shift AWAY from her voice; what it cannot carry is the plural identity. And 'lands exactly on the tier-4 heading' is a provenance inference, not a byte finding: the heading catalog audits a claim AGAINST heading-leaning, it cannot establish that a row leaned on one, and tier-4 is never evidence in either direction. REFINED (2): the charge that the device note contradicts a recurrence claim is an object error - the note's disclaimer object is מַה דּוֹדֵ֣ךְ מִדּ֔וֹד (byte sweep: 1 verse book-wide, 2 in-verse, byte-identical), which is genuinely intra-verse-only. The real gap is a different object: the row quotes הַיָּפָ֖ה בַּנָּשִׁ֑ים (oshb:Song.5.9) inside its own run, and that IS a byte-tier cross-verse recurrence (byte sweep: 3 verses - MT 1:8, 5:9, 6:1), untier-labelled and undisclosed.
p02.remedy: In boundary_rationale, splice and tier-label הִשְׁבַּעְתָּֽנוּ (oshb:Song.5.9, byte tier) as the plural-speaker evidence, keeping the 2fs addressee marker as the shift-away-from-her warrant it actually is. Add a cross-seam disclosure sentence for the oath root shared with oshb:Song.5.8 (skeleton sweep: 5 verses; oath-only root, speech role named on each side), and add web:Song.5.8 to boundary_evidence_refs so the mirror holds. Tier-label the הַיָּפָ֖ה בַּנָּשִׁ֑ים vocative as a byte-tier recurrence (byte sweep: 3 verses) or drop the quoted run. Add nothing about the WEB voice heading in either direction. Cure test: every voice-IDENTITY word in the row must trace to an in-verse form that marks the SPEAKER, not the addressee, and every cross-verse recurrence sentence must name its object and its tier.

p02.challenge_claim: The daughters-attribution again rests on an addressee marker rather than the verse's plural-speaker forms; the mutual-belonging shape discipline is performed entirely in transliteration with neither rival spliced, one of them located by position instead of a coordinate inside the offset zone; and the closing-clause bond with the named rival is undisclosed and mis-weighted at tier.
p02.grounds: Three sub-claims verified, one mis-framed. VERIFIED: the cited דּוֹדֵ֔ךְ (oshb:Song.6.1, byte tier) marks only the addressee, while וּנְבַקְשֶׁ֖נּוּ (1cp) and עִמָּֽךְ (2fs) in the same verse (oshb:Song.6.1, byte tier) - the forms that actually make the speakers plural - go uncited; the same under-evidencing class as the MT 5:9 row, so this is a cluster-level pattern, not an isolated slip. VERIFIED: neither rival shape is spliced, against the engagement-class rule that pointed splices plus tier labels are mandatory for every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim; the attested rivals are דּוֹדִ֥י לִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י ל֔וֹ (oshb:Song.2.16, byte tier) and אֲנִ֣י לְדוֹדִ֔י וְעָלַ֖י תְּשׁוּקָתֽוֹ (oshb:Song.7.11 = web:Song.7.10, byte tier). VERIFIED and tier-corrected: the row's close הָרֹעֶ֖ה בַּשׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים (oshb:Song.6.3) and the rival's close הָרֹעֶ֖ה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּֽים (oshb:Song.2.16) are identical at SKELETON tier only (skeleton sweep: 2 verses; byte sweep: 1 verse each - they split on the shin dagesh), so this is a closer cross-verse bond than the word-order contrast the note actually draws, and any byte-identity claim there would be false. REFINED on framing: OL calls the missing coordinate an offset-zone disclosure failure, but the offset-zone rule binds STRUCTURED refs and the device note writes no ref at all, so no offset-zone violation occurs there. The actual violation is the register purge - 'held later in this part' is a positional/part reference where cross-row references must be verse-anchored. Also refined: the remark that a high confidence band 'sits oddly' here is taste, not defect - the row's close does rest on a tier-1 formula anchor that survives the bytes, and the confidence band is not challenged by this ruling.
p02.remedy: Splice both rival shapes into device_notes with tier labels and verse-anchored coordinates - דּוֹדִ֥י לִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י ל֔וֹ (oshb:Song.2.16, byte tier) and אֲנִ֣י לְדוֹדִ֔י וְעָלַ֖י תְּשׁוּקָתֽוֹ (oshb:Song.7.11 = web:Song.7.10, byte tier; the dual is mandatory there) - replacing 'held later in this part' entirely. Add the shared closing clause as a skeleton-tier bond (skeleton sweep: 2 verses; byte sweep: 1 verse each, splitting on the shin dagesh) rather than leaving the word-order contrast as the only stated relation. In boundary_rationale, cite וּנְבַקְשֶׁ֖נּוּ and עִמָּֽךְ (oshb:Song.6.1, byte tier) as the plural-speaker evidence. Cure tests: no positional or part reference survives in any field; every offset-zone coordinate written anywhere on the row carries a dual; and every recurrence sentence names its tier, with no byte-identity wording on the shin-dagesh pair.

p02.challenge_claim: LF and OL raise the SAME core defect - 'bounded on both sides by a person-form shift' fails on the front edge, since MT 6:9 and MT 6:10 are alike third-person feminine predication. OL adds two DISTINCT defects: the three-site recurrence is carried at a tier the row never names, and the 'ascending' label imports an element absent from the verse's own bytes.
p02.grounds: All three sustained on re-derivation. FRONT SEAM (same defect in both packets): the word-final-kaf audit finds zero 2fs forms in EITHER MT 6:9 or MT 6:10; MT 6:9 predicates הִיא֙ three times with the 3fs mappiq suffixes לְאִמָּ֔הּ / לְיֽוֹלַדְתָּ֑הּ (oshb:Song.6.9, byte tier), and MT 6:10 continues feminine-singular predication with הַנִּשְׁקָפָ֖ה (oshb:Song.6.10, byte tier). The last actual 2fs address in the neighbourhood is לְצַמָּתֵֽךְ (oshb:Song.6.7, byte tier), three verses earlier; the יוֹנָתִ֣י תַמָּתִ֔י epithets at MT 6:9 are 1cs-possessive, addressive in flavour but not address forms. The row's bilateral claim therefore holds on the BACK side only, where the 3fs-to-1cs shift into יָרַ֔דְתִּי (oshb:Song.6.11, byte tier) is real and correctly grounds that edge. What the front edge does carry is weaker and different from what the row asserts: the speaker's 1cs possessive epithets drop out after MT 6:9 and the form turns declarative-to-interrogative. TIER DEFECT (OL, distinct, upheld): the row's own מִי זֹ֥את (oshb:Song.6.10) is byte tier at 1 verse; the three-site count is an accent_stripped/skeleton object (sweep: 3 verses at both tiers - MT 3:6, 6:10, 8:5), and no tier is named, against the tier-disclosure standard that a skeleton-tier cohesion driver meets the byte-grounded bar ONLY with the tier honestly named. LABEL DEFECT (OL, distinct, upheld): 'ascending-question' imports a byte-absent element - the ascending verb is attested in מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ (oshb:Song.3.6, byte tier) and at MT 8:5 (word-bound skeleton sweep of that verb: 2 verses, MT 3:6 and MT 8:5) and is ABSENT from MT 6:10, whose participle is הַנִּשְׁקָפָ֖ה. OL's high severity is sustained rather than reduced: this is a single-verse row whose independent existence rests entirely on the front cut, and tier-3 SAMEKH corroboration cannot carry a boundary whose tier-1 evidence does not survive.
p02.remedy: Strike 'bounded on both sides by a person-form shift' from boundary_rationale. If the row survives the escalated boundary question, state the front-edge signals in their true terms - loss of the speaker's 1cs possessive epithets after MT 6:9, the declarative-to-interrogative form change, and the mi-zot formula anchor - and tier-label that recurrence as accent_stripped/skeleton (sweep: 3 verses), replacing 'ascending-question' with a label MT 6:10's own bytes carry (the participial who-is-this-who-looks-out class). Re-cut observed_substrate_signals to the surviving driver, and re-open rejected_alternative and confidence with it. Cure tests (the tests that killed the original): a word-final-kaf plus 1cs/3fs audit over MT 6:9-6:10 must not contradict any person-shift wording left on the row; every recurrence sentence must name its tier; and no element of a formula label may be asserted that a sweep of the row's own verse cannot find.

p02.challenge_claim: The row never argues its own front boundary: neither the rationale nor boundary_evidence_refs addresses why the row does not continue 6:12's voice, despite an available tier-1 warrant.
p02.grounds: Verified against the row and the bytes. boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative address only the verse's internal two-voice structure and the BACK seam; MT 6:12 appears nowhere on the row, and the refs-mirror check returns GREEN precisely because no out-of-span mention of 6:12 exists to mirror - the silence is total, not a citation slip. One collateral assertion in the LF item is itself byte-false and is NOT adopted: the row's offset-zone dual-cite discipline is not followed throughout (see the OL ruling on this row); the front-boundary finding survives that correction.

Splice וְנֶחֱזֶה בָּ֑ךְ (oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13, byte tier) into the crux sentence, tier-labelled, as the plural-speaker evidence being weighed against the 2mp תֶּחֱזוּ֙ - the crux stays HELD, not decided. Cure test (the test that killed the original is prose-side, not machine-side): a hand sweep of EVERY structured coordinate in EVERY field, not only boundary_evidence_refs, must show a dual or numeric qualifier on each, since the deterministic arm does not reach prose fields; and no unsupported universal may remain on the row.

p02.challenge_claim: The curly-quoted WEB citation for web:Song.7.1 = oshb:Song.7.2 substitutes a straight apostrophe for the source's curly apostrophe, breaking byte-verbatim fidelity inside an otherwise well-grounded wasf-boundary claim.
p02.grounds: The byte fact is confirmed; the framing and the scope are both wrong. Exact-substring test (no punctuation normalisation) of every curly-quoted WEB span in this cluster's seven rows against the staged WEB verse text: 10 spans tested, exactly 3 fail, all three by U+0027 standing where the source carries U+2019 - web:Song.7.1 = oshb:Song.7.2 (source reads “prince’s daughter!”), web:Song.7.10 = oshb:Song.7.11 (“I am my beloved’s.”) and web:Song.7.11 = oshb:Song.7.12 (“Let’s go out into the field.”); the other seven spans are exact, including both of P02-012's and the long adjuration span at web:Song.8.4. So the defect is real but it is a THREE-SITE CLASS, not the single site the challenge frames. Severity correction: the campaign's WEB-verbatim arm is punctuation-normalised BY DESIGN (it is a gloss-as-WEB detector) and returns GREEN on all seven rows, and the mandatory register rule governs the ENCLOSING curly double quotes plus an inline web: ref in the same field, which every row here satisfies; the straight apostrophes inside the row's own Hebrew glosses are correct under the same rule. Test the cure must pass: an exact-substring test with punctuation normalisation DISABLED of every curly-quoted span in the revised rows against the staged WEB verse text - the test that returned 3 failures out of 10 here must return 10 of 10.

p02.challenge_claim: The row states an arithmetically false numbering-space identity for the offset zone and leaves its front seam - the book's crosswalk seam - uncited, while the tier-1 gender marker its own signal key rests on runs unbroken across that cut.
p02.grounds: Defect 1 is the load-bearing one and is confirmed: boundary_rationale reads '(WEB ch 7 = MT 7:2-7:6)'. Re-derived from the crosswalk in both directions - WEB ch 7 holds 13 verses and maps to MT 7:2-7:14 (MT ch 7 holds 14); MT 7:2-7:6 is only this row's own span (= WEB 7:1-7:5). A false chapter-level identity written in the one zone where dual discipline binds hardest, and it is invisible to the machine arms: the structured-ref arithmetic and the prose-pair arm both return GREEN on this row because the falsehood is a CHAPTER-level statement in prose. Defect 2 upheld in part and refined: the front neighbour web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1 appears in no evidence ref and in no prose, while the 2fs addressee marker IS continuous across that cut - oshb:Song.7.1 = web:Song.6.13 carries שׁ֤וּבִי four times (2fs imperative) and וְנֶחֱזֶה בָּ֑ךְ (2fs suffix), byte tier, and the row's own opener oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1 reads מַה יָּפ֧וּ with 2fs פְעָמַ֛יִךְ, so only the suffixed-body-part sub-class begins at MT 7:2 and a tier-1 address marker straddles the front seam undisclosed. REFINED: OL's supporting sub-claim that the praise-exclamation CONSTRUCTION also straddles the cut does not hold at its own digit - the skeleton sweep OL cites (3 verses: MT 4:10, MT 7:2 = WEB 7:1, MT 7:7 = WEB 7:6) is a sweep of the mah-plus-yod-pe opener, an object that EXCLUDES MT 7:1; מַֽה תֶּחֱזוּ֙ at MT 7:1 shares only the bare interrogative particle, which is not that device. Right digit, wrong count-object for the straddle claim. Defect 3 upheld at low: מֶ֖לֶךְ אָס֥וּר at oshb:Song.7.6 = web:Song.7.5 is the anarthrous member of the melek-lexeme set (independently re-swept: 5 verses, MT 1:4, 1:12, 3:9, 3:11, 7:6), and the row's straight-quoted byte-tier gloss 'the king is held captive' imports the English witness's definiteness. Tier-4 audit only, never evidence in either direction: OL's note that the uncited front seam coincides with a WEB [SPEAKER] apparatus site is correctly labelled and correctly excluded from the warrant. Convergence: LF's item on this row is a DISTINCT defect from OL's - no overlap.
p02.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: delete the false parenthetical and state either the span-level relation already carried in boundary_evidence_refs or an arithmetically correct chapter statement (WEB ch 7 = MT 7:2-7:14). Test: re-derive the chapter mapping with the crosswalk in BOTH directions and confirm the 13/14 verse counts before any chapter-level identity is written - the arithmetic that killed the original, and one no validator arm performs on prose, so a GREEN suite re-run does not certify this cure. (2) boundary_evidence_refs: add the front-seam pair web:Song.6.13 = oshb:Song.7.1, and disclose in boundary_rationale that the 2fs addressee marker runs ACROSS the front cut while only the suffixed-body-part run begins at oshb:Song.7.2 = web:Song.7.1, with spliced byte-tier forms on both sides. Test: the front-seam claim must quote a gender-marked form on both sides of the cut, not on one. (3) Re-cut the MT 7:6 gloss to the anarthrous bytes.

p02.challenge_claim: strongest_rejected_alternative engages only the weaker back-fold rival and omits the stronger, undisclosed forward-fold rival into the second wasf run.
p02.grounds: Confirmed. The row's strongest_rejected_alternative addresses only attachment to the preceding wasf; the forward fold into the second wasf run (web:Song.7.7-Song.7.9 = oshb:Song.7.8-Song.7.10) is engaged nowhere in the row. LF's device object re-derived independently rather than reproduced: the skeleton sweep of the praise-exclamation opener returns exactly 3 verses - MT 4:10, MT 7:2 = WEB 7:1, MT 7:7 = WEB 7:6 - so מַה יָּפִית֙ וּמַה נָּעַ֔מְתְּ in the row's own verse shares its opener formula with the FIRST wasf's opener מַה יָּפ֧וּ (skeleton tier, named as such), which makes 'this verse OPENS a wasf run' the strongest available rival rather than the back-fold the row declined. Aggravating and found independently here: the warrant offered on both sides is that 'the mechanically derived run ends at MT 7:6' - the derived wasf zone is a staging signal and is barred as row evidence, so the one rival the row does engage is refused on a non-evidentiary ground. NEW FINDING (neither primary): boundary_evidence_refs on this one-verse row carries its own verse and the PRECEDING span only - the forward neighbour web:Song.7.7 = oshb:Song.7.8 is absent, so the very seam the challenge concerns is uncited, and the row's seam citation is asymmetric. LF's tier-3 absence citation (no PE and no SAMEKH between MT 6:10 and MT 7:11) re-verified against the parashah inventory and correctly handled - absence is never counterevidence, and LF says so explicitly.
p02.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the back-fold sentence with the forward-fold rival (this verse as the opening exclamation of the wasf run at web:Song.7.7-Song.7.9 = oshb:Song.7.8-Song.7.10), declined on argued bytes; delete the derived-run appeal from the rationale and from the rival sentence alike; boundary_evidence_refs: add web:Song.7.7 = oshb:Song.7.8. Test the replacement warrant must pass - the test that killed the original: it must dispose of the 3-verse skeleton-tier opener formula (MT 4:10, MT 7:2 = WEB 7:1, MT 7:7 = WEB 7:6) on bytes alone, with no appeal to the mechanically derived run and no appeal to a speaker heading.

p02.challenge_claim: The single-verse cut is carried by a voice-shift signal key, but the bytes show no shift at all - same speaker, same 2fs addressee across MT 7:6-7:8 - and the vocative construal that supplies the only other warrant is undecidable on the staged evidence.
p02.grounds: The bytes are exactly as stated and the mislabel is real; the granularity framing over-reaches. CONFIRMED: oshb:Song.7.7 = web:Song.7.6 reads מַה יָּפִית֙ וּמַה נָּעַ֔מְתְּ - both perfects 2fs, carrying no final qamats where the 2ms counterparts would - flanked by 2fs body-part suffixes at oshb:Song.7.6 = web:Song.7.5 (רֹאשֵׁ֤ךְ עָלַ֨יִךְ֙) and oshb:Song.7.8 = web:Song.7.7 (קֽוֹמָתֵךְ֙), byte tier, with both witnesses reading one continuous address. No speaker change and no addressee change sits at either seam, so the observed_substrate_signals key voice_shift.transitional_address_exclamation is byte-false: the field contract requires the key to name the signal class actually consulted, and the class consulted here is a wasf form-class edge. REFINED (framing and severity): the conclusion that the cut is what the granularity rule forbids does not survive its own consequences - read that way the rule would equally forbid the two flanking wasf rows, which sit inside the SAME single voice; the owner's vocabulary makes wasf bounds writer-argued form-class seams (openers, closures, addressee shifts), so a wasf-to-non-wasf edge inside one voice is a licensed boundary. What is curable is the driver LABEL and the missing continuity disclosure, not the existence of the cut. Second defect upheld at low: 'as a vocative' for אַהֲבָ֖ה בַּתַּֽעֲנוּגִֽים is decided rather than held - the noun is anarthrous, no morphology layer is staged, and the rival construal (love as the exclamation's subject) stands on the same bytes, so the vocative reading tracks the English rendering and must be disclosed as held. Independently re-derived and CLEAN: the row's digit claim 'one of the ten ahavah-noun sites (sweep: 10 verses)' - the bare skeleton sweep returns 15 verses, less the 5 she-ahavah relative-verb formula verses (MT 1:7, 3:1-4), leaving 10 noun sites including MT 7:7; object correctly split, digit correct. Convergence: LF's item and OL's are DISTINCT defects at the same seam - a missing rival versus a byte-false driver key - and together they show one underlying weakness, that the isolation rests on a staging signal plus a mislabelled key rather than on bytes.
p02.remedy: observed_substrate_signals: replace the voice_shift.* key with a wasf form-class key (e.g. wasf.form_class_edge_non_body_part), and re-open every field the contract makes dependent on a driver swap - boundary_rationale, strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type, confidence. boundary_rationale must state that speaker and 2fs addressee are CONTINUOUS across both seams, with spliced byte-tier forms from oshb:Song.7.6 = web:Song.7.5, oshb:Song.7.7 = web:Song.7.6 and oshb:Song.7.8 = web:Song.7.7, and must hold the ahavah vocative construal open instead of asserting it. Test the cure must pass: no voice_shift.* key may stand on this row unless a gender-marked form or an attested formula anchor CHANGES at one of its seams - the test the original key fails.

p02.challenge_claim: The row's own last verse carries her address-word for him, undisclosed, contradicting the row's single-voice attribution and binding that verse forward into the mutual-belonging refrain across the row's back seam.
p02.grounds: Upheld on bytes. oshb:Song.7.10 = web:Song.7.9 - the row's own final verse - reads הוֹלֵ֥ךְ לְדוֹדִ֖י לְמֵישָׁרִ֑ים (byte tier); dodi is her word for him and is a tier-1 address vocabulary under the owner's moderate voice-attribution policy. The row is typed wasf_poem on the single signal key wasf.body_part_run_2fs_suffixes and quotes only that verse's closing three words דּוֹבֵ֖ב שִׂפְתֵ֥י יְשֵׁנִֽים, never the dodi clause. Both witnesses carry it - WEB renders “that goes down smoothly for my beloved” at web:Song.7.9 = oshb:Song.7.10 - so this is not an apparatus artefact. The token then repeats immediately across the back seam as אֲנִ֣י לְדוֹדִ֔י at oshb:Song.7.11 = web:Song.7.10, and the independent skeleton sweep of that exact form returns 5 verses (MT 5:5, 5:6, 6:3, 7:10 = WEB 7:9, 7:11 = WEB 7:10): a byte-true tier-1 device straddling the row's own seam, which argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed. The row's back-seam warrant instead rests on imagery class plus 'matching the mechanically derived wasf boundary exactly', a staging signal barred as row evidence. REFINED sub-claim: the inference that the voice turn therefore sits INSIDE oshb:Song.7.10 = web:Song.7.9 is a construal the staged evidence cannot decide - no morphology layer is staged and both witnesses admit either the man taking up her word or her interjection - so it is held, not adopted. CONVERGENCE, and the decisive one in this cluster: LF SUPPORTED this row, certifying that both WEB quotes are byte-verbatim and that the live forward rival is correctly engaged, and LF's own evidence field quotes the closing run of oshb:Song.7.10 = web:Song.7.9 IN FULL, dodi clause included, without flagging it. The two primaries are not addressing the same defect: LF found none, and LF's support is itself defective. Tier-4 audit only, never evidence: OL's note that the chosen back seam coincides with a WEB [SPEAKER] apparatus site before web:Song.7.10 = oshb:Song.7.11 is correctly labelled non-evidential and is recorded solely as an audit against heading-leaning at the one seam where the row's own Hebrew runs the other way.
p02.remedy: boundary_rationale must disclose the dodi token at oshb:Song.7.10 = web:Song.7.9 with a spliced byte-tier form, state how the unit's voice attribution survives a token of the OTHER address vocabulary standing inside its own span, and disclose the repetition at oshb:Song.7.11 = web:Song.7.10 as cross-seam cohesion; strongest_rejected_alternative must decline the forward extension without the derived-run appeal; device_notes must name the swept object precisely (dodi-exact, not dod-family) wherever a dod digit is used. Test the cure must pass: delete the derived-run sentence and the revised back-seam warrant must still stand, and it must dispose of the 5-verse skeleton-tier chain of that exact form across the seam - the two supports the original never faced.

p02.challenge_claim: LF: an unscoped 'hapax' universal claim lacking the mandated digit-bearing sweep disclosure, plus the apostrophe defect. OL: the row names a Hebrew form that is not in its span - MT 7:13 reads the 1cs defective dodai, not a 2ms 'dodekha' - and its mandrake and cohortative labels are likewise off the bytes.
p02.grounds: Upheld, and the severity rises above both primaries' medium: the lead defect is a Hebrew FORM named in row prose that the cited bytes do not carry, standing in the very row that owns the token, in the book whose signature hazard is dod-family blending. CONFIRMED (the form): oshb:Song.7.13 = web:Song.7.12 reads אֶת דֹּדַ֖י לָֽךְ (byte tier). The attested token is דֹּדַ֖י - 1cs, no second-person suffix in the consonants at all - and both witnesses read the speaker's own possessive (WEB “There I will give you my love.” at web:Song.7.12 = oshb:Song.7.13), whereas device_notes calls it 'the defective-spelling dodekha token', a 2ms form absent from these bytes. Re-swept independently: the defective spelling returns exactly 4 verses (MT 1:2, 1:4, 4:10, 7:13 = WEB 1:2, 1:4, 4:10, 7:12); MT 1:2 and 1:4 carry a 2ms suffix and MT 4:10 the 2fs דֹדַ֖יִךְ, so MT 7:13 is the single member whose suffix runs the other way - wrong form and wrong direction of address in the row that argues who addresses whom. CONVERGENT, the SAME defect from both primaries: 'the mandrakes hapax' carries no scope and no digit. Re-swept: הַֽדּוּדָאִ֣ים returns 1 verse in this book (MT 7:14 = WEB 7:13); the staged evidence supports only a book-scoped digit, and 'hapax' is a universal claim requiring the adjacent digit-bearing citation that names object and unit. The automated universal arm does not carry 'hapax' in its claim vocabulary, so this class is reachable only by review - and both primaries reached it. CONFIRMED (the form labels): 'One sustained 1cs voice' and 'her single cohortative address' mis-state the run - the cohortatives in the span are first-person PLURAL, נֵצֵ֣א and נָלִ֖ינָה at oshb:Song.7.12 = web:Song.7.11 and נַשְׁכִּ֨ימָה֙ and נִרְאֶ֞ה at oshb:Song.7.13 = web:Song.7.12, while the genuinely 1cs forms are אֶתֵּ֥ן and צָפַ֥נְתִּי; the automated universal arm independently flagged the word 'single' in that same sentence. The signal key voice_shift.1cs_cohortative_invitation inherits the error. LF's apostrophe half is confirmed (web:Song.7.11 = oshb:Song.7.12 reads “Let’s go out into the field.”) but belongs to the three-site class cured by one sweep.
p02.remedy: device_notes: name the MT 7:13 token by its attested form - the 1cs defective spelling, spliced, byte tier, dual-cited oshb:Song.7.13 = web:Song.7.12 - and state the direction of address it actually carries; scope the mandrakes claim to the book with its digit ('sweep: 1 verse in this book'). boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative: replace 1cs with 1cp for the cohortative chain and re-key observed_substrate_signals accordingly, re-opening rationale, rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence as dependents of the driver swap. boundary_evidence_refs: add the back-seam pair web:Song.7.13 = oshb:Song.7.14 | web:Song.8.1, currently uncited on both sides. Test the cure must pass: every Hebrew FORM named in prose must be re-spliced from its cited verse and re-collated at byte tier before the row ships - the check both 'dodekha' and '1cs cohortative' fail - and the mandrakes scope must carry a digit naming object and unit.

p02.challenge_claim: OL: the rival dialogue reading is rejected on a ground the bytes contest, and the book's only two wall-noun sites sit on either side of the row's own back seam, undisclosed. (LF supported this row.)
p02.grounds: The load-bearing half is upheld; the framing half is corrected. UPHELD: חוֹמָ֣ה (oshb:Song.8.9) and חוֹמָ֔ה (oshb:Song.8.10) are the lexeme's only two sites in the book (skeleton sweep: 2 verses), they are adjacent, and they are identical only once cantillation is stripped (byte tier at each ref, accent_stripped tier as a pair). The answer is clause-for-clause: אִם חוֹמָ֣ה הִ֔יא is answered by אֲנִ֣י חוֹמָ֔ה, and וְשָׁדַ֖יִם אֵ֣ין לָ֑הּ is answered by וְשָׁדַ֖י כַּמִּגְדָּל֑וֹת (byte tier at their own refs). That byte-true device straddles the row's own back seam with nothing in the prose disclosing it, while web:Song.8.10-Song.8.12 sits in boundary_evidence_refs without ever being argued. REFINED: the challenge says the bytes contest the stated ground; they do not. 'One speaker-group without an answering party' is byte-true of the span's interior - oshb:Song.8.8 carries לָ֨נוּ֙, נַּעֲשֶׂה֙, לַאֲחֹתֵ֔נוּ and oshb:Song.8.9 carries נִבְנֶ֥ה and נָצ֥וּר, all 1cp, all byte tier. The corrected finding is that the rejected alternative engages the wrong rival: the live rival the bytes make available is a Song.8.8-Song.8.10 dialogue_exchange, not a Song.8.8-Song.8.9 one, and the row never reaches it. LF's support of this row is independently verified and not contradicted (see supported_sample): the 1cp front seam and the achot role-split are both sound, and the back seam survives the straddling device because the 1cp-to-1cs person change at oshb:Song.8.9|8.10 is in-verse and marked.
p02.remedy: Disclose the straddling wall-noun and breast answer at the Song.8.9|8.10 seam in boundary_rationale, splicing both sides at byte tier and naming the tiers honestly (byte at each ref; identical only at accent_stripped tier as a pair), and state why the seam survives it - the marked 1cp-to-1cs person change. Replace the rejected alternative's rival with a Song.8.8-Song.8.10 dialogue_exchange, within the one-sentence limit. Either argue web:Song.8.10-Song.8.12 in prose or drop the ref. NEW (neither packet): the identification of the speaker-group AS the brothers is carried by content inference alone - no in-verse form names them - while the byte anchor that would carry it sits unused at oshb:Song.1.6, בְּנֵ֧י אִמִּ֣י (byte tier), the same verse that supplies the keeper-and-vineyard chain linking oshb:Song.1.6, oshb:Song.8.11 and oshb:Song.8.12 (skeleton sweep: 3 verses); cite it or lower the attribution's stated tier. TESTS the cure must pass: (1) no byte-true device straddles the row's seam undisclosed; (2) the rejected alternative names the strongest rival the bytes make available; (3) every attribution states the tier that carries it.

p02.challenge_claim: OL: the quoted marker is a common-gender pronoun and cannot carry the row's return to her own voice, the verse's actual gender-bearing forms go unquoted, and the petuchah is placed inside the verse rather than at the division it closes. (LF supported this row, calling the pronoun an unambiguous tier-1 marker and the mark correctly disclosed.)
p02.grounds: Upheld on both counts, and LF's support is refuted in part. אֲנִ֣י (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier) fixes person and number only; set against the 1cp נִבְנֶ֥ה and נָצ֥וּר of oshb:Song.8.9 (byte tier) it is genuine tier-1 evidence for a SPEAKER change, so the seam itself stands and LF is right that far - but the owner voice policy requires the gender-marked form to be quoted for the attribution, and this verse's gender-bearing forms sit unquoted inside it: כְּמוֹצְאֵ֥ת, a feminine-singular participle, בְעֵינָ֖יו, a 3ms suffix locating the other party as a man, and וְשָׁדַ֖י כַּמִּגְדָּל֑וֹת answering oshb:Song.8.8 (all byte tier). Second count, also upheld: the mark inventory is verse-keyed and this cluster's own rows read a seg as closing its verse - the setumah at MT 8:4 is cited as the front seam of Song.8.5, the setumah at MT 8:7 as the front seam of Song.8.8 - so the book's single petuchah at MT 8:10 corroborates the MT 8:10|8:11 division, which is this row's BACK seam, not the front seam the row attaches it to; and 'sitting exactly at this pronoun-marked return' is an intra-verse position claim a verse-keyed single-witness inventory cannot source. The 1-of-20 digit, the petuchah-versus-setumah distinction and the single-witness disclosure are correct, and the mark is not treated as the driver.
p02.remedy: Splice כְּמוֹצְאֵ֥ת שָׁלֽוֹם and בְעֵינָ֖יו (oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier) into the seam warrant so the attribution rests on a gender-marked form, keeping אֲנִ֣י as the person-and-number marker it actually is. Re-cut the parashah sentence to the division the seg closes (MT 8:10|8:11) and delete the intra-verse placement; the dependent signal key must move from a self-marker to a back-seam key, since the driver framing changed. Re-open confidence, which was set above its siblings on the strength of the marker now corrected. p02.challenge_claim: LF: the Hebrew quote excludes 'chaverim' yet the attached gloss translates it - a quote/gloss same-span violation. p02.grounds: Two findings on one row: the parity defect is the SAME defect in both packets; OL's marker-thinness finding is DISTINCT and additional; both upheld. The digit for that address vocabulary is 24 verses in its attested exact spellings, and the object matters: a contiguous-consonant sweep returns 25 because it also catches דּוֹדִֽים at oshb:Song.5.1, which is the lovers-noun, not her address word - the five-object dod trap, avoided here. Tier-4: no WEB speaker heading is relied on by either packet or by this ruling, in either direction.
p02.remedy: Re-cut the gloss to its run, or extend the run to include חֲבֵרִ֛ים and re-collate to byte tier, and drop the 2fs-imperative label from the masculine-plural participle. Replace the thin-markers warrant with the hold-whole warrant, quoting the לְקוֹלֵ֖ךְ against לְךָ֤ pair and דּוֹדִ֗י at byte tier and naming the address-vocabulary digit with its object (exact attested spellings, sweep: 24 verses). TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS: every voice-shift seam claim quotes the gender-marked Hebrew form, spliced and tier-labeled, and a genderless rendering cannot carry it; no byte-true device may straddle either of the row's seams undisclosed; and the speech-role split must be stated in the same terms the row already uses to keep the adjuration site count at four.

boss_docket.challenge_claim: OL's DISTINCT sub-claim on the same row: an undisclosed byte-identical inclusio straddles the row's back seam, arguing the praise frame closes at 6:10 rather than at 6:9.
boss_docket.grounds: The bytes are verified and the disclosure defect is real: אֲיֻמָּ֖ה כַּנִּדְגָּלֽוֹת closes oshb:Song.6.4 and closes oshb:Song.6.10 byte-identically (byte sweep: 2 verses book-wide), and בָּרָ֥ה הִ֖יא (oshb:Song.6.9) / בָּרָה֙ (oshb:Song.6.10) cross the same seam - a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam, undisclosed, which the cross-seam cohesion rule says argues continuity against the row. boss_docket.challenge_claim: Both primaries: the row cuts a continuous single-voice run at the WEB chapter 7|8 boundary with no tier-1 voice-shift marker at the cut and never engages the live merger rival with the preceding row (LF, high). OL adds an entirely uncited front seam, a quote/gloss parity break at 8:3, and an untiered recurrence claim that is not byte-identical to its counterpart.
